title: Add latency-watermark sampler and changelog tiler for compact release drafts
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Introduce a sampled latency-watermark profiler and a changelog tiler that produce concise, impact-scoped release drafts from telemetry; adds a minimal metadata contract field for telemetry requirements and a backfill CLI helper. No breaking changes.
commits_summary: 4 commits: initial watermark sampler and schema (latency_watermark.go + v2_contract.yaml), changelog tiler implementation (changelog/tiler.py) and tests, backfill/migration CLI, docs and sample profiles; fix lint and edge cases after review.
description: Context: We want more compact, representative release notes and better per-model performance anchors without storing full telemetry dumps. Motivation: teams are overwhelmed by large per-model telemetry and the release assembler often pulls noisy metrics. This PR adds two coordinated pieces: (1) a latency-watermark sampler that records a small set of statistically representative tail watermarks (median, p90, p95, p99) across segmented workloads using reservoir sampling and weighted decay; and (2) a changelog tiler that consumes sampled telemetry + onboard annotations to produce compact, impact-scoped tiles used by the release assembler. Design details: the sampler is implemented as an incremental recorder (onboard/sampler/latency_watermark.go) and emits a compact payload (max ~5 numeric anchors) that is merged into model profiles under profiles.schema.v2.telemetry_contract.watermarks. The telemetry contract schema (profiles/schema/v2_contract.yaml) introduces a required_keys list (e.g. request_id, duration_ms, model_variant) and a contract.version field so we can evolve telemetry expectations. The changelog tiler (changelog/tiler.py) groups change candidates into tiles: performance, cost, compatibility, and docs. Tiles include a short sentence, a numeric delta when applicable, and sample anchor(s) from the watermarks to make statements like "p95 latency improved 18% for chat-16k on long prompts". Migration/backfill: a small CLI (cmd/onboard/backfill_telemetry.go) scans existing profiles and runs the sampler over a bounded historical window (configurable by days) to create watermarks for profiles that lack them. Rollout plan: enable sampling for new onboard flows behind feature flag --enable-watermark-sampler; backfill in a controlled batch for existing models; expose the tiler output in a new REST endpoint /profiles/{id}/release-tiles. Testing: unit tests for statistical properties and edge cases (tests/sampler/latency_watermark_test.go) and an integration test for tiler assembly (tests/tiler/tiler_integration_test.py). Performance: sampler is designed to be O(1) per sample and caps memory per-profile to ~200 items during sampling windows. Checklist: - [x] Add sampler implementation and tests - [x] Add changelog tiler and integration test - [x] Add telemetry_contract schema and docs - [x] Add backfill CLI and safety knobs (rate limit, window days) - [x] Add REST route and auth checks - [x] Docs and migration notes Related: ENG-3420 (sampling infrastructure), PM-118 (release notes UX), SUP-839 (support case: noisy changelog drafts). Follow-ups: expose watermarks in the Console UI as latency anchors; add a small evaluator that flags regression tiles automatically; experiment with sampling weights based on traffic buckets. CI: initial runs flagged a flaky tiler test (timing), fixed by adding deterministic seeding in tests; final CI is green. Merge: squash-merged to main after approvals and a quick canary backfill run in staging.
